prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Your Desktop Pet", "Select a desktop companion to begin your onboarding journey."]
1: ["Meet Your Future Desktop Pet", "Your companion lives on your screen, reacts to your activity, and offers daily encouragement."]
2: ["Desktop Pet Controls", "Click to talk, right-click for quick settings, or drag to reposition your pet anywhere on your screen."]
3: ["Welcome to Your Desktop Companion", "Choose how you want your pet companion to fit into your daily desktop workflow."]
4: ["Signing in links your desktop pet to your account so progress is never lost."]
5: ["We will alert you as soon as your desktop companion completes spawning."]
6: ["Your Pet is Live on Desktop!", "Left-click your pet to open interactions, or right-click to hide or adjust desktop companion settings."]
7: ["Includes Starter Accessories & Expressions"]
8: ["Building Desktop Pet Graphics..."]
9: ["Select Your Pet Experience"]

verdicts.problem: mentions free extras or included items
